newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil 1996 trade deficit seen at $5 bln - CNI.
newsitem.headline: Brazil 1996 trade deficit seen at $5 bln - CNI.

text.p: Brazil's trade deficit for 1996 should be larger than expected at $5 billion, the private National Industry Confederation (CNI) said.
CNI said the trade gaps in the last two months of the year were likely to be lower than October's record $1.3 billion.
The high trade deficits in recent months reflect, in part, a reduction in exports, especially of manufactured goods, it said.
The amount of manufactured goods available for export is declining due to an expanding domestic market and limited production capacity, CNI said.
Production capacity needs new investment in order to grow, it said.
Exports will only increase in line with imports once the cost of doing business in Brazil is further reduced, allowing companies to raise investments, it said.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro Newsroom 5521 507 4151
